The street at every hour and in every weather

WorldStreetApproved 2026-11-262 issues seen
Locks
The example street of real lots from World/ (building_kit_07): the café's awning and its lit windows, the facades' relief raked by the sun, the far rows closing it in haze; street lamps lit at dusk and on the lamp-lit night, dark on the moonlit nights; the full moon a cool light, a new moon only stars. Rain as the game's (Game/README Weather): thin pale streaks (4.5 mm), the open paving darker with a faint sheen in half-metre cells, soft-edged dark puddles with a little mirror and faint grey rings; none under a roof or arch. Snow lies only under open sky.

The sky and its clouds at every hour and in every weather

WorldSkyApproved 2026-11-262 issues seen
Locks
The sky over the town, seen from Market Square over the roofs: blue overhead fading to the pale haze at the horizon by day, warm towards the low sun at dusk, the night's dark blue with the town's glow low down; clouds as soft heaps on one layer about 1.2 km up, flat underneath and rounded on top, lit on the sun's side and shaded underneath, pink at dusk, lit from below by the town's lamps at night; how much of the sky they cover follows the weather (clear 0.36, cloudy 0.62, rain 0.97, fog 0.55, snow 0.92); at night the stars, the Milky Way and the full moon's disc. No planet (ADR-0064).

The old-town alley at every hour and in every weather

WorldAlleyApproved 2026-11-262 issues seen
Locks
The look of the world (the old-town alley of style test 02: matte mottled plaster and stone, soft rounded forms, W1-W8) at morning, midday and dusk; at night with the lamps on, and with them off under a full and a new moon; and by day in cloud, rain, fog and snow. No haze at midday. Rain and snow fall, puddles lie with rings where the drops fall into them, and the snow lies, only where the sky is open over them: never under the passage's roof. Only the light and the weather change between them. Rain as the game's (Game/README Weather): thin pale streaks (4.5 mm), the open paving darker with a faint sheen in half-metre cells, soft-edged dark puddles with a little mirror and faint grey rings; none under a roof or arch.

The kinds of light and their named colours, in a home's room at night

IndoorLightKindsFor your review9 issues seen
Locks
The named colours of light of World/rules/lights.json and the fittings that share them (the owner, 2026-11-26: "when the room is lit by lights then the color should be decided by the light types"; "each colored light should have a name for different styles of lamps, lights, street lights etc. can share the color behavior"). Ten colours: Lantern amber (the palette's Lantern, for street lamps and lanterns to share), Warm white, Soft white, Neutral white, Cool white, Fire red, Neon blue, Neon green, Neon red, Neon amber (the owner: "we also need some cooler and even neon blue and green lights"; "add those 3 suggestions"). Thirteen fittings, each lit alone in the approved home room (IndoorHomeRoom) on a night with no moon and the fire out: floor lamp, table lamp, wall light and pendant in Warm white, desk lamp in Soft white, ceiling light in Neutral white, cool ceiling light in Cool white, wall lantern in Lantern amber, candles in Fire red (every fire one red, candles too: the owner, "Fire red"). Neon is an accent (the owner: "Weaker neon"): a tube of 8 to 10 W, shown with the room's own floor lamp, table lamp and fire lit, so the room keeps its colours and the tube tints its corner. A fitting's strength is its own; its colour is its named colour's. The sheet shows each fitting twice: at one exposure for all (the lamp-lit night's), and with the eye set for that light, at most 2.5 stops either way; each fitting has its own entry under Ornaments (OrnamentsLight<Fitting>), with the second picture.
Approved
proposed 2026-11-26, for the owner to review; pictures at low quality until approved
Decision
ADR-0065, ADR-0067; the owner, 2026-11-26, of the colours and fittings on a trial sheet: "Yes, propose it"
Made by
Tools/blender/light_kinds_54.py (on the home room of Tools/blender/hours_50.py and furniture_kit_18.py), the sheet by Tools/blender/light_kinds_54_sheet.py
Models built from it
  • World/rules/lights.json (the colours and the fittings)
  • Game/Source/BrixTown (the rooms' lamps: not built to this yet, FURN-066, FURN-067)
Rules
docs/specs/domains/FURNITURE.md 2.5, docs/art/ART_DIRECTION.md 2.3 and 2.6

Seen wrong, for the owner to judge

  • Night only: dusk and the day hours are not shown for these lights.
  • Neon blue, green and red are saturated colours, against the palette rule W4 (muted and warm); allowed as weak accents by the owner's words (ADR-0067).
  • Neon amber is hard to tell from the fire-lit room it is shown in; neon red reads pink and tints more of the room than the other tubes at the same strength.
  • The pendant and both ceiling lights burn out at the shared exposure and flatten the room (little shade under the furniture); with the eye set for them they are not burnt but still flat.
  • Floor lamp, table lamp and desk lamp look alike: Soft white is barely different from Warm white.
  • Candles at the shared exposure are almost black; with the eye opened the room goes orange-red. They are lit at 3 W, as the hour script lights every fire, where the file says 6 W.
  • The room holds every fitting at once, so its walls are crowded with unlit tubes and wall fittings; the floor lamp and the desk lamp stand behind the person.
  • The wall light, the wall lantern, the ceiling lights and the neon tubes are simple fittings made for this reference; the furniture kits have none, and they are not approved pieces.
  • Every colour value and strength is an [ASSUMPTION] in lights.json until this is approved. Tried and dropped: neon tubes of 30 to 40 W alone in the room (the whole room one colour, as a filter); candles in a colour of their own (1.0, 0.60, 0.28).

A home's room (the living room) at every hour

IndoorHomeRoomApproved 2026-11-264 issues seen
Locks
The living of furniture_kit_18, closed on four sides with one window. In the world's light (the owner, 2026-11-26: "use the same color etc from world lighting"): by day only the sun and sky of the hour, through the window, with the sunlit street outside throwing its light in; lamps and the fire out by day; the boards a greyer wood, so the bounced light is not orange; at night the lamps a warm white (until the kinds of light, FURN-066), the fire lit, the full moon a cool patch through the window, a new moon only the window's starlight. No weather settings indoors (the owner). The wall facing the people throws light back onto them (the owner, 2026-11-26: "the wall opposite to the character is not reflecting light back"): by day a little of the day through the window, at night a share of the lamps' light in their colour. Every fire, in every reference, one red (the owner, 2026-11-26: "oven flame should be same color in all references and more red"): its flames glow red and catch no light; with no other light in a room its red takes the room over, as it should (the owner). Two more nights with the fire out as well as the lamps (the owner: "we need reference of moon lights when the fire place is turned off"): the full moon only through the window, dim and cool, a new moon very dark.

Eastgate Mall's moving stairs close by, at every hour

MallsEastgateEscalatorsApproved 2026-11-285 issues seen
Locks
Every moving stair in Eastgate Mall, shown at the foot of the pair in the Great Court's middle. Their shapes are the game's: the plan's ramps (World/city_01/blocks/b_16_5.json, b_16_5_l0: from a to b, 4.4 m wide, floor to floor, 6 m over 29 m), with the game's parapet down the middle (BrixMall.cpp, 0.3 m wide) making two lanes of about 1.8 m. Close by, in the court's look (MallsEastgateCourt, ADR-0069): at each end a fixed floor plate of darker steel with a thin brass edge and a dark comb where the steps slide under it; two flat steps, then steps of 0.2 m up the slope; dark grey treads and risers, ribbed along the way they travel, mostly not metal so the sun through the roof lights shows on them, a thin brass line on each step's nose; polished steel skirts with a line of light along their top; a cream deck; glass sides ending in round newels with a brass handrail along their top and round each newel; the middle parapet the same, a steel skirt and line of light to each lane, a cream deck and a glass side with its handrail to each lane; the outside clad in the galleries' timber slats, a cream edge and a line of light along its foot; the underside in the same slats. In the world's light: at Midday the sun through the middle roof light falls on the upper part of the stairs; in the Morning and at Dusk it is too low to reach them; at dusk and at night the lines of light and the hall's lanterns at full. No moonlit nights, no weather.

How the references are kept

  • Every approved look reference is in Art/Reference/<Category>/, named <Category><Subject>[_<Variant>].<ext> in PascalCase: Indoor/IndoorHomeRoom_Morning.jpg, Vehicles/VehiclesSoftBox.png. A reference's id is the name without the variant.
  • Art/Reference/catalog.json is the one list: what each locks, its approval and decision, the script that makes it, the game models built from it, issues seen, its old names. Agents read it there.
  • This page is written from it by python Tools/reference_catalog.py, which first checks that every file is listed and named by the rule. Never edit the page by hand.
  • A new reference: render it with its script, put it in its category's folder under its name, add it to the catalog, run the script. Changing the look needs a new ADR and the owner's approval (ADR-0004).
  • A reference taken out of use moves to Art/Retired/ and is listed under Retired.
  • Look tests and rejected ideas stay in Art/StyleTests/; they are not references.
